# Campus Library Reservation System  
## Architecture and Quality Plan

## 1. Context and scope

The Campus Library Reservation System (CLRS) will replace the university’s existing study-room reservation tool. It will support students and staff across three libraries, including room searching, reservation management, recurring staff block bookings, kiosk displays, reminders and utilisation reports.

The system must integrate with the university’s SAML identity provider, facilities iCal feeds and a read-only PostgreSQL room-inventory database. The design covers the first release and focuses on the reservation, availability, kiosk and reporting capabilities described in the requirements. It does not include implementation code, replacement of the identity provider, or modification of the legacy inventory database.

The most important architectural concerns are reliable reservation rules, availability search performance, integration isolation, kiosk freshness, security, straightforward testing and operational simplicity. The system will be deployed and maintained by a two-person team, so excessive deployment and service-management complexity is undesirable.

This document selects hexagonal architecture as the primary architectural style. The domain and application logic will be isolated from external technologies through ports and adapters. A single deployable application will initially be used, with asynchronous processing for notifications and kiosk updates where appropriate.

The first release covers the stated functional requirements: room search, reservation management, staff block bookings, kiosk schedules, reminders and reports. It does not include replacement of the identity provider, changes to the legacy inventory database or implementation of a new campus-wide calendar.

The principal architectural concerns are availability, search performance, secure authentication and auditing, configuration-based onboarding of new campuses, testability of reservation rules, and operational simplicity for a two-person team. The proposed design therefore prioritises a simple deployment model while isolating the domain logic from infrastructure dependencies.

# Campus Library Reservation System (CLRS)  
## Architecture and Quality Plan

## 1. Context and scope

The Campus Library Reservation System (CLRS) will replace the university’s ageing study-room reservation tool. It will support students and library staff across three campuses. Students must be able to search for rooms and equipment, create, modify and cancel reservations, while staff must manage rooms, opening hours, recurring block bookings and utilisation reports. Kiosks located outside rooms must display the current and next reservation.

CLRS integrates with three existing systems:

- The university identity provider through SAML.
- Facilities calendars through iCal feeds.
- A read-only PostgreSQL room-inventory database.

The primary quality objectives are:

- **QR-1 Availability:** 99.5% monthly availability during opening hours, with kiosks showing their last-known schedule when offline.
- **QR-2 Performance:** availability searches at p95 under 400 ms for 2,000 concurrent users.
- **QR-3 Security:** SAML authentication for all user actions, audited staff actions and no personally identifiable information in logs.
- **QR-4 Modifiability:** a new campus can be added through configuration only.
- **QR-5 Testability:** reservation rules
